quizzes.title: Telegram ban: misuse and blocking context
quizzes.passage: Telegram, a messaging platform, has come under scrutiny in India after the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) temporarily blocked it under Section 69A of the Information Technology Act, 2000. The action followed reports that criminal groups had used Telegram's message-editing feature to target and defraud candidates appearing in the NEET-UG 2026 Re-Examination. Fraudsters reportedly inserted fake exam papers into old messages after an exam had ended, creating a false appearance of a pre-exam leak and spreading misinformation. The platform's privacy features add to the concern. Hidden phone numbers and end-to-end encryption in secret chats make it nearly impossible for investigators to trace malicious actors. The platform also permits the sharing of massive files, which makes it easy to distribute high-resolution PDFs of leaked documents. Telegram hosts active marketplaces for renting bank accounts used in money laundering, extortion, and illegal gambling. Criminals use automated bots to distribute illegal content and coordinate large-scale activities with minimal manual effort. Government data shows a sharp increase in official cybercrime complaints linked to activities organised within Telegram groups. Section 69A empowers the Central Government, or an officer it specially authorises, to direct any government agency or intermediary to block public access to online information. The episode shows how platform features can be misused for organised fraud against candidates.

quizzes.title: Section 69A: powers and safeguards
quizzes.passage: Section 69A of the Information Technology Act, 2000 is the main legal mechanism the government uses to restrict access to digital content and online platforms in India. It empowers the Central Government, or an officer it specially authorises, to direct any government agency or intermediary to block public access to online information. Requests for blocking are examined under the Information Technology (Blocking Rules) through a structured review process. Before a proposed action is put into effect, it is checked for its necessity and legality. In urgent situations, however, the government may act before a full review is completed, provided the action is examined later. Blocking decisions must fall within specific grounds that concern the nation, its security, and public peace. These grounds include the sovereignty and integrity of India, the defence of India, and public order. The power is meant to deal with organised crime and harmful content online, but it must also respect constitutional freedoms and judicial scrutiny. Such a framework helps the state balance security concerns with the rights of individuals and platforms. Many disputes over blocking have reached the courts, which have examined both the powers and the safeguards. Officials who use the power and platforms that receive such directions are both expected to follow the prescribed procedure carefully.

quizzes.title: Revision and PPI: MCQ Practice
quizzes.passage: Price indices are widely used to track inflation, and the Wholesale Price Index (WPI) is a key measure among them. The Government of India has now approved a revision of the WPI base year, moving the reference point of the index to a more recent period. A base year is the reference period against which later price movements are measured, so changing it allows the index to reflect the structure of the modern economy more accurately. Economic activity has changed considerably since the earlier base year was fixed. The revision therefore aims to capture these shifts in the composition of goods, in the way they are classified and in the way their relative importance is measured. Accurate measurement matters because the WPI sits early in the supply chain, and its movements often signal pressures that may later reach consumers. Alongside the revised WPI, the Government has decided to introduce new Producer Price Indices. These indices are meant to give a wider picture of the prices that producers receive and pay, and of the costs they face in production. Together, the revised series is expected to provide a more complete view of inflation at the producer level, helping policymakers, businesses and analysts read cost and price dynamics with greater confidence.

quizzes.title: Producer Indices: Typed Answer Practice
quizzes.passage: Most discussion of inflation focuses on the prices that households pay, yet the prices that producers receive and pay also shape the economy. Policymakers therefore need measures that show price movements from the producer's side of the chain. Economic activity today is also not limited to physical goods. The service sector is also part of economic activity, and a separate Service Producer Price Index tracks its prices. A measure that covers only goods can leave important producer-side changes out of view. To address such gaps, the Government has decided to introduce a new family of producer indices alongside the revised wholesale index. The indices are intended to capture price changes at different stages of production and across services as well. They are also expected to help analysts understand cost conditions and supply-side pressures faced by businesses. Because producers operate in many sectors, a broader set of indices allows a more detailed reading of how cost and revenue pressures move through the economy. Such information can help central planners, investors and industry bodies anticipate changes in inflation before they fully appear in consumer prices.

quizzes.title: G7 Evolution Check
quizzes.passage: The Group of Seven, commonly called the G7, did not begin as a fixed club of advanced economies. It was set up as a response to a period of unsettled global economics and a major energy shock, when leading industrialised nations felt the need to consult closely with one another. The original group was a small circle of Western and Asian economies, and it later added a new member that turned the forum into a larger body for some years. Afterwards, the membership changed again when one participant's involvement was halted. The forum then returned to its earlier arrangement, which remains in place today. Each phase reshaped the membership, but the group's consultative purpose stayed the same over the decades. Throughout these changes, the grouping has kept its informal character, meeting to discuss pressing economic, political and strategic questions rather than operating as a formal treaty organisation. The history of the G7 therefore shows how a forum can grow, shrink and reorganise in response to global events while keeping its core purpose of consultation. The forum brings together some of the world's most advanced industrialised economies. The chronology also helps explain the forum's present-day role as a platform for consultation among major economies.

quizzes.title: Membership and Structure Check
quizzes.passage: The Group of Seven is an informal forum that brings together some of the world's most advanced industrialised economies. Its purpose is to serve as a platform for consultations on major economic, political and strategic issues facing the world today. Because it is informal, it does not function like a treaty-based international organisation with binding rules. Instead, its members meet to share views, compare national positions and look for common ground. Several other actors take part in the group's deliberations, including international bodies that are closely involved in its discussions, although they do not share the same status as the core members. The forum is led in turn by its members, so that each country takes its turn at hosting and guiding the agenda for a set period before handing over responsibility to the next. This system of rotation ensures that leadership is shared and that different national priorities are represented over time. Successive leaders have shaped the forum's agenda since it was formed. Each feature of the forum, including its composition, its rotating leadership and its informal nature, helps explain how the grouping works in practice. Its ability to bring together major economies also gives its discussions weight across many policy areas.

quizzes.title: Quad at a glance: MCQ set
quizzes.passage:
The Quad is a grouping of India, the United States, Japan and Australia that has grown from a set of humanitarian contacts into a diplomatic grouping. Its roots lie in cooperation that followed a devastating disaster in the Indian Ocean region. A Japanese leader later gave the idea a sharper political shape, and the grouping was revitalised in response to growing unease about the expanding military and economic presence of a large regional power in the Indo-Pacific.

Today the Quad works as an informal strategic partnership rather than a formal alliance. Its stated aim is a region that is free, open, inclusive, secure and prosperous, anchored in the rule of law, freedom of navigation, territorial integrity and the peaceful resolution of disputes. These principles are applied in practice through specific initiatives, each with its own focus areas and objectives.

The eleventh foreign ministers' meeting of the group turned these ideas into concrete outcomes across several areas. Maritime cooperation is one strand, with shared surveillance tools and data arrangements focused initially on the Indian Ocean. Other outcomes cover critical minerals, energy, undersea connectivity, digital identity systems and agriculture. Many of these efforts aim to reduce dependence on a few suppliers and to build resilient supply chains and infrastructure across the region.

quizzes.title: Economy and technology: typed answers
quizzes.passage:
Economic security has become a central part of the Quad's agenda. Members have recognised that depending on a small number of suppliers for essential raw materials can create supply vulnerabilities, so they are working to spread sources more widely. Cooperation now spans the full life cycle of key minerals, from mining and processing to recycling, with the aim of making supply less exposed to shocks.

Energy is another priority. The group has agreed to a joint regional approach that links energy technology, supply chain strength and the assessment of market risks. This work is meant to help countries across the Indo-Pacific manage market risks.

The Pacific islands are also part of the agenda. A planned outreach effort aims to link island nations of the Pacific Islands Forum through a more robust network and to modernise ports, with completion targeted for the near term.

On technology, the Quad is developing practical tools for digital systems. Officials are preparing a reference document that will help public and private platforms work with one another across borders. A separate initiative uses artificial intelligence, robotics and remote sensing to support farming and food security. Together these efforts seek to make growth in the region both secure and resilient.

quizzes.title: E85 Basics Check
quizzes.passage: India is considering a policy framework to make the adoption of E85 fuel affordable. Ethanol is a highly purified alcohol that can be blended with petrol and used as a transport fuel. Ethanol blending means mixing ethanol with petrol to create fuel that can run internal combustion engines. The idea is to lower the country's reliance on imported crude oil while giving farmers a steady market for their produce. Ethanol is derived from plant-based sources, and the wider family of biofuels also includes fuels made from animal waste. The Ethanol Blending Programme began as a pilot and was later widened under a national policy on biofuels. The programme set a target of blending twenty per cent ethanol, written as E20. Officials also stress environmental gains, since ethanol replaces fossil fuels and lowers greenhouse gas emissions. E85 is a fuel blend that carries much more ethanol than ordinary petrol, and the policy discussion is about making it affordable. Read together, these points show how energy security, farm incomes and cleaner air are linked in the rollout of ethanol fuels. The discussion also considers rural livelihoods, since farmers supply the raw material that makes the fuel possible. Supporters argue that ethanol stocks can help manage prices when crude oil costs rise sharply. Critics, however, raise questions about how crops diverted to fuel affect food supply and whether ordinary vehicle owners will see lower running costs. Any framework that aims for affordable adoption must balance these competing concerns while keeping the programme's environmental goals in view.

quizzes.title: Policies and Schemes Check
quizzes.passage: India's biofuel effort rests on several policy instruments. The National Policy on Biofuels aims to reduce import dependence by promoting blends of bioethanol, biodiesel and bio-CNG. One scheme provides financial assistance for second-generation ethanol made from surplus biomass and agricultural waste. Another scheme focuses on managing cattle dung and solid waste on farms and turning them into useful products. A separate policy aims to create bio-foundries that would produce biotechnology-developed feedstock and catalysts, and planned enzyme production would support existing and proposed ethanol plants in several states. India also joined partners to launch an alliance focused on sustainable biofuels and cooperation between countries. Another initiative aims to build an ecosystem that collects used cooking oil and converts it into biodiesel. The Cabinet has approved a hydrogen mission with targets for green hydrogen capacity, renewable energy capacity addition and jobs. Taken together, these measures show how biofuel policy spans agriculture, energy, waste management and international cooperation. Policy design in this area also looks at farm residue, since stubble and dung can be turned into fuel and compost.

quizzes.title: Forests, Wetlands and Wildlife Drives
quizzes.passage: India's efforts to protect its green cover combine large national missions with focused local drives. The National Mission for Green India concentrates on expanding forest and tree cover while also improving the quality of the cover that already exists. Funds for compensatory afforestation are managed by a dedicated authority, which supports regeneration on degraded land. India also protects its wetlands, and several of these are recognised as Ramsar Sites. Two major programmes were started to protect large wild animals, one focused on tigers and another on elephants. Along the coastline, mangroves are being promoted through a national initiative that seeks to support both habitats and local livelihoods. The Aravalli Green Wall is a planned green belt along a mountain range. Public participation is also encouraged, and campaigns invite ordinary people to plant trees as part of the effort. India further publishes a periodic national report on the condition of its forests. Taken together, these measures show how planning, public funds, wildlife protection and citizen action work side by side to protect the natural environment.

quizzes.title: Plastics, Cleanliness and Mission LiFE
quizzes.passage: Plastic pollution is a pressing environmental problem, and governments are negotiating a legally binding agreement to end it worldwide. A dedicated negotiating committee has been meeting for this purpose, holding its sessions in different countries as the talks progress. India has added its own domestic efforts. A cleanliness campaign that began as a national drive has grown into a mass movement with the aim of building a clean and green India. Business and conservation groups have also joined hands in a plastics pact that seeks to transform the packaging value chain across all formats and products. A project called REPLAN works on the same problem from another direction, collecting waste plastic and processing it so that it can be turned into something useful. Mission LiFE, described as an India-led global mass movement, encourages individuals and communities to take small, sustainable actions that protect the environment. The mission also sets targets for villages and urban local bodies to become environment-friendly, showing that ambition is set at the local level as well as the national level. Together, these initiatives show that solving plastic pollution requires government negotiations, industry commitment, local innovation and changes in everyday habits.

quizzes.title: Defence and Nuclear Developments
quizzes.passage:
Defence and nuclear developments featured prominently this month. The annual SIPRI Yearbook 2026, published by the Stockholm International Peace Research Institute, highlights rising global militarisation, nuclear modernisation and India's evolving nuclear posture. It reports that India's defence expenditure rose to USD 92.1 billion in 2025, placing India among the world's largest military spenders.

India's nuclear decision-making rests on its Nuclear Command Authority, which has two bodies. The Political Council is the sole body authorised to release nuclear weapons, while the Executive Council provides inputs to it and executes its directives.

On air defence, India has received the fourth squadron of the S-400 Triumf system from Russia, which is designated Sudarshan in Indian service. India has also signed a deal to supply BrahMos supersonic cruise missiles to Vietnam, as announced during the Shangri-La Dialogue. BrahMos was used in combat for the first time during Operation Sindoor.

Globally, military spending reached USD 2.9 trillion in 2025, marking the 11th consecutive year of growth. The world retained 12,187 nuclear warheads, and nuclear-armed states continue to rely on nuclear deterrence as a strategic tool. The Yearbook also notes that Ukraine recorded the highest military burden in the world, with its military spending equivalent to 40% of its GDP.

quizzes.title: Industry, Ports and Infrastructure
quizzes.passage:
India's industrial and infrastructure indicators drew attention this month. The Index of Industrial Production (IIP) recorded a growth of 4.9 per cent in April 2026, lower than the 5.8 per cent growth registered in April 2025. Manufacturing, which carries a large share of the index, expanded by 6.2 per cent, while mining and quarrying contracted. Alongside this, the government released a revised IIP series with 2022-23 as the new base year, replacing the earlier 2011-12 base.

On the logistics front, India released its Logistics Port Performance Index for FY 2024-25 along with four new digital governance initiatives. The index evaluates ports across dry bulk, liquid bulk and container cargo. Its key performance indicators include vessel turnaround time, berth idle time and container dwell time. The framework was developed by the Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways.

Road connectivity also advanced, as the Zojila Tunnel crossed a 13 km excavation milestone. The tunnel is part of an all-weather road link between Kashmir and Ladakh. The revised IIP series retains mining and quarrying, manufacturing and electricity as traditional sectors, while adding new activities such as gas supply, water supply and waste management. Electricity generation is now classified separately into renewable and non-renewable sources, which sharpens the picture of industrial output.
